Why each part of this store is here

Every component that tries to influence a purchase is listed below with the behavioural principle behind it, the research it rests on, when it is allowed to show, the effect we measure, and the rule that keeps it honest. A component shows only when its data is real.

ComponentPrincipleEvidenceShown only whenExpected effect and metricDark-pattern guard
Back In Stock Alert Commitment: a shopper who asks to be told is likely to come back and buy. Cialdini, 1984, on commitment and consistency. The variant has a Sellable_Quantity of 0 and the Back_In_Stock_Alert Optional_Feature is enabled. More Orders after alert emails; metric: Orders placed from alert emails. One email only, sent when the variant is back in stock. The request is deleted after sending or after 90 days, and the email address is used for nothing else.
Free Delivery Progress Goal gradient and loss clarity: showing the real distance to free delivery, the real saving and the real step helps shoppers finish. Baymard checkout research; Kivetz et al. on the goal-gradient effect. The threshold, the Prior_Price or Promotion, the pairing, the Bundle Promotion, the device history, the first-order Promotion or the checkout step exists in the Backend's data. Higher Cart value and checkout completion. Nothing is added to the Cart except by the add control of that product or offer. The First_Order_Offer shows once per session and not for 30 days after a close; its close control looks like its accept control.

Delivery Promise Certainty: a delivery date answers the shopper's question better than a shipping speed, which 41% of sites do not show (Baymard). [Baymard on shipping speed versus delivery date](https://baymard.com/blog/shipping-speed-vs-delivery-date). The shopper's PIN code is known and has a Serviceability_Rule with a delivery estimate. The dates use the store's working days, holidays and Dispatch_Cutoff; without current Live_Data the text gives working days only. More completed checkouts; metric: the Order placed step of the Storefront_Funnel. Dates come from Serviceability_Rules and working days only. A PIN code with no rule shows no date, and a code that cannot be served says so.
Dispatch Countdown A concrete deadline makes a benefit tangible, and slow delivery is a leading reason for abandoned checkouts (Baymard). [Baymard cart abandonment research](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate). A Dispatch_Cutoff is set, today is a working day in the Store_Timezone, the server time is before the cutoff, the selected variant is in stock (not backorder), and Live_Data is current. More checkout starts; metric: the checkout started step of the Storefront_Funnel. The deadline is the store's real cutoff, read against the server clock and not the device clock. It never shows after the cutoff or on a non-working day, and never resets. It hides under the stale rule and when the Component_Switch is off.
Low Stock Notice Scarcity: a real limit on supply speeds a decision. Cialdini (2009), Influence; Dark_Pattern guidelines on false urgency. The selected variant's Sellable_Quantity is above 0 and at or below the low-stock threshold, backorders are not allowed, and Live_Data is current. More checkout starts for scarce items. It states the exact quantity from the Backend, never a rounded or invented one, and never for a backorder variant. Hidden under the stale rule and when the Component_Switch is off.
Popularity Notice Social proof: seeing that many others bought reduces uncertainty. Cialdini (2009), Influence; Dark_Pattern guidelines on false popularity. The Backend band is 5 or more (the largest of 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1,000 at or below the 7-day Order count) and Live_Data is current. Higher conversion rate on product pages. The Store_API sends only the band, never the count, and a value outside the bands is ignored. Hidden under the stale rule and when the Component_Switch is off.
Price Block Price transparency and reference pricing: a shopper judges a price against a real earlier price (Prior_Price), and a clear total saving reads as one gain. Indian law requires the MRP and a unit sale price where they apply. Reference-price effects on perceived value (Thaler, 1985, mental accounting); Dark_Pattern guidelines on drip pricing and false discounts ([Grant Thornton summary](https://www.grantthornton.in/globalassets/1.-member-firms/india/assets/pdfs/dark_pattern_flyer_2024.pdf)). The Prior_Price and the saving show only while the backend supplies a Prior_Price above the current price (a Price_Reduction). The tier table shows only when the variant has quantity tiers. The unit price shows only when the Business_Preset requires it. More Cart additions from product views; metric: View_To_Cart_Rate. No struck-through price or saving outside a Price_Reduction; the MRP is never struck through and never gives a saving; the saving is rounded down; the stale price shows a note that the Cart confirms the price.
Review Highlights Balanced social proof: a critical review beside a positive one makes the positive one credible. Spiegel Research Center (2017); Dark_Pattern guidelines on fake or selected reviews. Both a published 4-5 star and a published 1-3 star review of at least 100 characters exist; the newest of each shows. Higher conversion rate and fewer returns. Reviews are shown unedited and as plain text. A critical review always accompanies a positive one. Hidden when the Component_Switch is off.
Review Summary Social proof: shoppers use other buyers' ratings to judge quality. Cialdini (2009), Influence; Spiegel Research Center (2017) on reviews and purchase likelihood. The product has at least 1 published review; the rating and count come from the Backend summary. Higher conversion rate on product pages. Nothing shows without a published review. The average is rounded to 1 decimal and never invented. Hidden when the Component_Switch is off.
Sale Countdown Loss aversion: losses weigh about twice as much as equal gains (Tversky and Kahneman, 1992), so a real deadline on a real price makes the offer concrete. Tversky and Kahneman (1992), cumulative prospect theory; Dark_Pattern guidelines on false urgency ([Grant Thornton summary](https://www.grantthornton.in/globalassets/1.-member-firms/india/assets/pdfs/dark_pattern_flyer_2024.pdf)). Live_Data supplies the end of the Price_List or Promotion that gives the current price, the end is within 48 hours of the server time, and Live_Data is current. It hides when the end passes. More Orders during sales; metrics: conversion rate and Orders during sales. The time left comes from the server clock, not the device clock. The countdown never restarts for the same Price_List or Promotion, shows the later price, and gives the end time as static text. It hides under the stale rule and when the Component_Switch is off.
Trust Strip Risk reduction: stating real guarantees lowers perceived risk at the point of decision. Baymard research on trust at checkout; Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules. Store_Settings and the Backend confirm the statement for the product and the shopper's postal code: secure payment, Cash_On_Delivery, return window, GST invoice, country of origin. Higher conversion rate and fewer abandoned checkouts. Each statement needs its own confirmed evidence; none is a fixed claim. Hidden when no statement is confirmed or the Component_Switch is off.

Layout choices

  • One orange primary button per screen. A single high-contrast action is easier to find (isolation effect) and fewer choices speed decisions (Hick's law).
  • Wide search in the header, cart on the right. Shoppers scan the top bar left to right; search is the main way large-catalogue stores (Amazon.in, Flipkart) are used.
  • Trust strip under the hero. Returns, delivery and payment safety answer the top three non-price reasons people abandon (Baymard).
  • Full price, delivery charge and savings before checkout. Surprise costs are the biggest single reason for abandonment (40%, Baymard).
  • Picture-led category tiles. Used by Myntra and Nykaa to get shoppers into a category in one tap on phones.

Sources

  • Baymard Institute: cart abandonment (70% average; 40% leave over extra costs, 20% over slow delivery, 19% over trust)
  • Baymard Institute: checkout usability research
  • Nielsen Norman Group: search box and F-pattern scanning
  • Cialdini, Influence (1984): social proof, scarcity, commitment, reciprocity
  • Government of India: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

Every component can be switched off in the Admin_App, and its real effect is measured with an Experiment (control against treatment) before it stays on.
